summary.headline: Star Cement Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to Rs 164 crore from Rs 194 crore, with PAT down to Rs 39.58 crore from Rs 71 crore.
summary.overview: Cement sales volume rose to 11.23 lakh ton from 10.72 lakh ton YoY, but revenue of Rs 831 crore (vs Rs 811 crore) did not translate into profit, with EBITDA per tonne at Rs 1,372 vs Rs 1,651. Management attributed weak Q2 demand to elections and floods in Assam, its core market. For H1, EBITDA was Rs 367 crore (vs Rs 424 crore) and PAT Rs 113 crore (vs Rs 169 crore). Management expects H2 volume growth of 12-13% and is working to cut fuel cost to about Rs 1.45 per unit by March. Capex for the new capacity was revised up, with the Nimbol project now guided at about Rs 3,080 crore total.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 811 crore in Q2 FY26
Flat vs Q1 per call; guided to fall to Rs 1.45 by March

segments.name: Cement (North East)
segments.commentary: Sold 7.96 lakh ton in Q2 FY27 vs 7.84 lakh ton a year ago; management says North East industry growth in H2 will be 7-8%, with Star growing above 10%. Trade share was 77%.

segments.name: Cement (outside North East, incl. West Bengal)
segments.commentary: Sold 3.27 lakh ton vs 2.88 lakh ton YoY, about 13.5% growth. West Bengal demand is described as strong.

segments.name: Clinker
segments.commentary: Sold 0.74 lakh ton in Q2 FY27 vs 1.01 lakh ton a year ago. Management says clinker is sold selectively to smaller non-branded cement makers, and clinker prices were raised.

segments.name: Non-cement revenue
segments.commentary: Rs 22 crore in Q2; about Rs 37-38 crore in H1, with about Rs 100 crore expected for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Cement plus clinker volume growth of 12-13% YoY expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27; management said October cement volume growth was above 12%.
Full-year FY27 cement volume growth target of about 7-8% as stated on the call.
Fuel cost per unit guided to fall from Rs 1.52 to about Rs 1.45 by end of March 2027.
Rajasthan-equivalent eastern unit: Nimbol 3.3 Mtpa clinker plus 3 Mtpa cement and 3 Mtpa grinding (up from 2 Mtpa), with commissioning around July-August 2028.
Management reaffirmed that the FY27 EBITDA guidance will be achieved by year-end, though the range was not restated in the call.
Incentive subsidy expected at about Rs 65 crore per half year for the next two halves, following the Assam incentive policy change.
capex_capacity: Capex in H1 FY27 was about Rs 203 crore. The Q1 presentation had Rs 560 crore for FY27, Rs 1,500 crore for FY28 and Rs 1,910 crore for FY29, with the total for the Nimbol project now about Rs 3,080 crore. Management said the Q1 presentation numbers broadly still hold.

Nimbol environmental clearance was being sought around October-November 2026 per management. Capex phasing across FY28/FY29 is flexible, depending on the use of the deferred-payment (BIS-type) import window.
Railway siding at Nimbol: power partly connected; rail siding expected by January 2027, after which freight savings should begin.
Grinding unit at Siliguri: decision expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27. Viha is deferred if Siliguri proceeds, with the plot kept for later use.
Management said a 20 Mtpa capacity target could be reached around 2030-2032. Management said it is not considering a QIP for the time being.
demand_pricing: Management said Q2 demand was weak due to elections and Assam floods; Q3 and Q4 are seeing better traction.
Prices in North East were flat in September and rose about Rs 10/bag in October. Outside North East (West Bengal) prices rose about Rs 10-15/bag.
Management said the North East market has about 15 million tonnes of annual demand, with the 15-16% share served by rail at roughly 2.4 million tonnes per year.

Management expects three large entrants (Ambuja, JK Lakshmi, Shree Cement) to be 2028-2029 supply, with about 1.5 Mtpa of annual demand growth. Management said Star's North East dominance and margins should hold for about two years.
Premium share (PPC/PSC-type blended mix) was about 17.3% and green power about 28% of energy. FSA about 45% of fuel mix. Blended power cost was Rs 2.15/unit.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see H2 volume and October demand trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 cement plus clinker volume growth is expected at about 12-13% YoY, and October cement volume growth was above 12%. Pent-up demand from Q2 is expected to show up in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation trend in North East and outside?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices in September were flat. October saw about Rs 10/bag increase in North East and Rs 10-15/bag in areas outside North East, including West Bengal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fuel cost still at about Rs 1.52-1.55 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel cost fell to Rs 1.52 in Q2 from Rs 1.55 and will reach Rs 1.45 by March. Alternative fuel (AFR) availability was an issue; coal prices are rising into Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the incentive income rise to about Rs 36 crore in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Assam incentive policy change approved for the remaining 12 years drove a one-time boost. Subsidy is expected at about Rs 65 crore per half year in the next two halves.

qa_highlights.question: Will Star keep the FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 1,500-1,600/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA guidance will be achieved by year-end. No revised figure was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the North East industry set to face more volatility from new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants are coming for margins but the market is not large. Star's share of North East is one of the highest; some capacity may be rationalised. Management does not see a margin pressure problem for two years.

risks_watch: Fuel cost: management needs to bring it from about Rs 1.52 to Rs 1.45/unit by March 2027 amid rising coal premiums (per analyst question).
Capex for Nimbol rose to Rs 3,080 crore and the FY29 phasing may shift to FY28 or FY30 depending on deferred-payment import options.
Competition: Ambuja, JK Lakshmi and Shree Cement entering North East from 2028-2029 could pressure prices.
Incentive income is sensitive to the Assam policy change; the Rs 36 crore booked in Q2 may not repeat at the same level.
Clinker sales fell to 0.74 lakh ton from 1.01 lakh ton; management said selling clinker will be more selective from Q3 with prices raised.
Q2 EBITDA per tonne fell to Rs 1,372 from Rs 1,651, and PAT halved; the EBITDA guidance was not restated.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on H2 volume recovery and North East dominance, but cautious on the Q2 margin squeeze, fuel cost and capex phasing. Several answers on capex and fuel were vague or inconsistent, and the transcript quality limits precision.

adds.what: Nimbol (eastern unit) 3.3 Mtpa clinker plus 3 Mtpa cement and 3 Mtpa grinding (up from 2 Mtpa)
Grinding unit at Siliguri (decision pending; Viha deferred if it proceeds)

growth.why: Management guides Q3-Q4 cement plus clinker volume growth of 12-13% and FY27 cement volume growth of 7-8% (cut), backed by October volumes up over 12%, price increases of about Rs 10-15/bag, and the Nimbol 3 Mtpa cement unit (commissioning around July-August 2028) with capex raised to about Rs 1,910 crore for FY27-FY29; Q2 EBITDA fell 15.5% YoY on weak demand from elections and Assam floods.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Fuel cost is guided to fall from Rs 1.52 to about Rs 1.45/unit by March 2027 and prices rose about Rs 10/bag in NE and Rs 10-15/bag outside NE in October, but coal prices are rising and the Rs 36 crore incentive in Q2 is one-off, so EBITDA/t recovery is conditional.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nimbol 3 Mtpa cement unit (part of 3.3 Mtpa clinker plus 3 Mtpa grinding) is under construction with commissioning guided around July-August 2028 and Rs 203 crore capex spent in H1 FY27, so no new capacity lands in the next 2-4 quarters beyond the Nimbol rail siding and Siliguri decision.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides cement plus clinker volume growth of 12-13% YoY in Q3 and Q4 with October cement volume up above 12%, though FY27 cement growth is cut to 7-8% and Q2 volume rose only ~4.8% (11.23 vs 10.72 lakh ton).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Siliguri grinding unit decision is expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 and Nimbol capex was raised to about Rs 3,080 crore total, with FY27 phasing of Rs 560 crore still to be spent.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the Rs 1,500-1,600/t EBITDA guide without raising it, and H1 EBITDA/t was Rs 1,438 versus Rs 1,716 a year ago.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 cement volume growth was cut to 7-8%, Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs 1,372/t from Rs 1,651/t, and the FY27 EBITDA/t guide of Rs 1,500-1,600 was reaffirmed without a restated range while fuel is still Rs 1.52 per unit.

rows.label: Realisation hikes in October
rows.why: Prices rose about Rs 10/bag in North East and Rs 10-15/bag in West Bengal in October after flat September prices, supporting H2 realisations.

rows.label: Incentive subsidy from Assam policy
rows.why: Subsidy is guided at about Rs 65 crore per half year for the next two halves, versus the Rs 36 crore booked in Q2 that was partly one-time.

rows.label: Rail siding at Nimbol
rows.why: Rail siding expected by January 2027, after which freight savings should begin, though the size of savings was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 volume recovery (Oct volumes above 12%) and North East dominance, but cautious on Q2 margin squeeze, fuel cost and Nimbol capex phasing; analysts pressed on fuel, the incentive one-off and the FY27 EBITDA guide, which was not restated.
